{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment within the existing Spring XD architecture and preserve backward compatibility for existing stream, job, module, and deployment definitions wherever practical.",
    "Use the Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE dependency set specified in U5 as the compatibility baseline, including the explicitly listed transitive and related dependency versions.",
    "Expose HDFS Avro compression through configuration, using the existing Avro codec configuration mechanism where possible; support disabling compression and selecting a codec without changing existing defaults.",
    "Pass JavaMail SSL/TLS properties through the existing Mail sink java-mail-properties mechanism and support both secure IMAP and secure SMTP through standard JavaMail protocols and properties.",
    "Expose partitionResultsTimeout as metadata for every applicable job, including all three out-of-the-box jobs that import the single-step partitioning strategy.",
    "Implement deployment manifest properties as a separately referenced YAML file while retaining support for existing inline stream-definition properties.",
    "Implement message compression using a self-describing content-encoding convention so consumers can determine whether and how to decompress a message.",
    "Support gzip and zip compression and decompression through reusable compression components rather than duplicating logic in each module.",
    "Apply the compression capability to both Rabbit source and Rabbit sink modules, preserving uncompressed operation as the default for compatibility.",
    "Use automated unit, integration, configuration, and regression tests, supplemented by a repeatable Sqoop versus jdbchdfs benchmark procedure for U1.",
    "Treat documentation, sample configurations, metadata definitions, and release validation as part of the increment rather than as post-release activities."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The existing Spring XD source repository, build infrastructure, module framework, metadata system, and test harness are available and can be built locally.",
    "The requested work targets the historical Spring XD codebase associated with Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE; migration to current Spring Framework or Spring Boot versions is out of scope.",
    "No major redesign of the Spring XD runtime, transport protocol, HDFS storage format, or deployment subsystem is required.",
    "The three out-of-the-box jobs referenced by U4 can be identified from the repository and require only metadata and configuration exposure, not changes to their business logic.",
    "A usable Hadoop/HDFS test environment, RabbitMQ instance, mail server or mock mail server, and representative Sqoop and jdbchdfs datasets are available or can be provisioned using existing project facilities.",
    "For U1, the benchmark deliverable consists of repeatable benchmark scripts or configuration, execution against representative data, and a comparison report; production optimization of either batch job is out of scope.",
    "For U2, existing Avro file writing and codec libraries are retained, and the requested codec setting is passed through configuration rather than implementing new compression algorithms.",
    "For U3, JavaMail's standard SSL/TLS support is sufficient; certificate-authority, client-certificate, and custom trust-store administration are not treated as separate product features.",
    "For U6, YAML parsing and file-loading libraries already available in the application can be used, with validation for malformed or missing manifest properties.",
    "For U7 and U8, compressed messages carry an encoding indicator or equivalent metadata, and interoperability is required only between the updated Spring XD modules unless existing protocol conventions already define compatibility.",
    "Zip support is implemented for a single logical message payload rather than multi-entry archive management.",
    "Dependency upgrade work includes resolving compilation, test, packaging, and obvious runtime compatibility issues caused by the specified versions, but excludes unrelated cleanup or upgrades not required by U5.",
    "The estimate is for one developer performing implementation, testing, documentation, integration, and release preparation; it represents work-hours and not elapsed calendar time."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Repository analysis and increment design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing modules, build structure, metadata model, job definitions, HDFS and Mail sinks, Rabbit source and sink, deployment processing, and benchmark facilities. Produce an implementation plan and identify compatibility impacts across U1-U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Sqoop versus jdbchdfs benchmark deliverable",
      "activity_description": "Define comparable benchmark scenarios and metrics, prepare repeatable data and execution configurations, run both batch jobs, collect performance statistics, and document the comparison and limitations.",
      "most_likely_effort": 36
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "HDFS Avro codec configuration",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration to disable Snappy compression and select an alternate Avro codec for the hdfs-dataset sink, update validation and defaults, and add focused unit and integration tests for compressed and uncompressed Avro output.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Mail sink TLS and secure protocol support",
      "activity_description": "Integrate JavaMail SSL/TLS properties and secure IMAP/SMTP protocol handling with the Mail sink configuration, verify property propagation, and test secure and non-secure connection paths using mocks or an available test server.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Partition results timeout metadata exposure",
      "activity_description": "Expose partitionResultsTimeout as metadata for the single-step partitioning strategy and ensure the property is available through all applicable importing jobs, including the three identified out-of-the-box jobs. Add metadata and job configuration regression tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Spring Boot and dependency upgrade",
      "activity_description": "Update the parent and dependency versions to Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE and the complete specified dependency set, resolve build and API incompatibilities, update affected configuration, and execute the existing test and packaging suites.",
      "most_likely_effort": 96
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "External YAML deployment manifest support",
      "activity_description": "Add parsing, validation, loading, and lifecycle integration for a separate YAML deployment-manifest properties file. Preserve existing inline definitions, handle missing or malformed files, and add unit, integration, and example configuration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Reusable gzip and zip message compression",
      "activity_description": "Design and implement reusable compression and decompression components for gzip and zip, define content-encoding behavior, handle invalid or unsupported encodings, and add round-trip, compatibility, and error-path tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 88
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Rabbit source and sink compression integration",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration and runtime integration of the reusable compression capability to Rabbit source and sink modules, including compressed publishing, decompression on receipt, uncompressed defaults, message metadata handling, and Rabbit integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 48
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature regression and integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and test suites, exercise representative end-to-end stream and job scenarios, verify backward compatibility of existing definitions, and diagnose and fix integration defects across the eight user stories.",
      "most_likely_effort": 72
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Documentation, metadata, and examples",
      "activity_description": "Update reference documentation, module and job metadata, configuration descriptions, YAML manifest examples, TLS examples, Avro codec examples, and Rabbit compression usage guidance.",
      "most_likely_effort": 28
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Packaging and release validation",
      "activity_description": "Validate Maven artifacts, module packaging, dependency resolution, generated metadata, upgrade and clean-install behavior, and prepare release notes or change summaries for the increment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 536
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment within the existing Spring XD architecture and preserve backward compatibility for existing stream, job, module, and deployment definitions wherever practical.
Use the Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE dependency set specified in U5 as the compatibility baseline, including the explicitly listed transitive and related dependency versions.

Expose HDFS Avro compression through configuration, using the existing Avro codec configuration mechanism where possible; support disabling compression and selecting a codec without changing existing defaults.
Pass JavaMail SSL/TLS properties through the existing Mail sink java-mail-properties mechanism and support both secure IMAP and secure SMTP through standard JavaMail protocols and properties.
Expose partitionResultsTimeout as metadata for every applicable job, including all three out-of-the-box jobs that import the single-step partitioning strategy.
Implement deployment manifest properties as a separately referenced YAML file while retaining support for existing inline stream-definition properties.
Implement message compression using a self-describing content-encoding convention so consumers can determine whether and how to decompress a message.
Support gzip and zip compression and decompression through reusable compression components rather than duplicating logic in each module.
Apply the compression capability to both Rabbit source and Rabbit sink modules, preserving uncompressed operation as the default for compatibility.
Use automated unit, integration, configuration, and regression tests, supplemented by a repeatable Sqoop versus jdbchdfs benchmark procedure for U1.
Treat documentation, sample configurations, metadata definitions, and release validation as part of the increment rather than as post-release activities.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source repository, build infrastructure, module framework, metadata system, and test harness are available and can be built locally.
The requested work targets the historical Spring XD codebase associated with Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE; migration to current Spring Framework or Spring Boot versions is out of scope.
No major redesign of the Spring XD runtime, transport protocol, HDFS storage format, or deployment subsystem is required.
The three out-of-the-box jobs referenced by U4 can be identified from the repository and require only metadata and configuration exposure, not changes to their business logic.

A usable Hadoop/HDFS test environment, RabbitMQ instance, mail server or mock mail server, and representative Sqoop and jdbchdfs datasets are available or can be provisioned using existing project facilities.

For U1, the benchmark deliverable consists of repeatable benchmark scripts or configuration, execution against representative data, and a comparison report; production optimization of either batch job is out of scope.
For U2, existing Avro file writing and codec libraries are retained, and the requested codec setting is passed through configuration rather than implementing new compression algorithms.
For U3, JavaMail's standard SSL/TLS support is sufficient; certificate-authority, client-certificate, and custom trust-store administration are not treated as separate product features.
For U6, YAML parsing and file-loading libraries already available in the application can be used, with validation for malformed or missing manifest properties.

For U7 and U8, compressed messages carry an encoding indicator or equivalent metadata, and interoperability is required only between the updated Spring XD modules unless existing protocol conventions already define compatibility.
Zip support is implemented for a single logical message payload rather than multi-entry archive management.

Dependency upgrade work includes resolving compilation, test, packaging, and obvious runtime compatibility issues caused by the specified versions, but excludes unrelated cleanup or upgrades not required by U5.
The estimate is for one developer performing implementation, testing, documentation, integration, and release preparation; it represents work-hours and not elapsed calendar time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing modules, build structure, metadata model, job definitions, HDFS and Mail sinks, Rabbit source and sink, deployment processing, and benchmark facilities. Produce an implementation plan and identify compatibility impacts across U1-U8.

Define comparable benchmark scenarios and metrics, prepare repeatable data and execution configurations, run both batch jobs, collect performance statistics, and document the comparison and limitations.

Add configuration to disable Snappy compression and select an alternate Avro codec for the hdfs-dataset sink, update validation and defaults, and add focused unit and integration tests for compressed and uncompressed Avro output.

activities.activity_name: Mail sink TLS and secure protocol support
activities.activity_description: Integrate JavaMail SSL/TLS properties and secure IMAP/SMTP protocol handling with the Mail sink configuration, verify property propagation, and test secure and non-secure connection paths using mocks or an available test server.

Expose partitionResultsTimeout as metadata for the single-step partitioning strategy and ensure the property is available through all applicable importing jobs, including the three identified out-of-the-box jobs. Add metadata and job configuration regression tests.

Update the parent and dependency versions to Spring Boot 1.2.0 RELEASE and the complete specified dependency set, resolve build and API incompatibilities, update affected configuration, and execute the existing test and packaging suites.

Add parsing, validation, loading, and lifecycle integration for a separate YAML deployment-manifest properties file. Preserve existing inline definitions, handle missing or malformed files, and add unit, integration, and example configuration tests.

activities.activity_name: Reusable gzip and zip message compression
activities.activity_description: Design and implement reusable compression and decompression components for gzip and zip, define content-encoding behavior, handle invalid or unsupported encodings, and add round-trip, compatibility, and error-path tests.

activities.activity_name: Rabbit source and sink compression integration
activities.activity_description: Add configuration and runtime integration of the reusable compression capability to Rabbit source and sink modules, including compressed publishing, decompression on receipt, uncompressed defaults, message metadata handling, and Rabbit integration tests.

Run the complete build and test suites, exercise representative end-to-end stream and job scenarios, verify backward compatibility of existing definitions, and diagnose and fix integration defects across the eight user stories.
Update reference documentation, module and job metadata, configuration descriptions, YAML manifest examples, TLS examples, Avro codec examples, and Rabbit compression usage guidance.
Validate Maven artifacts, module packaging, dependency resolution, generated metadata, upgrade and clean-install behavior, and prepare release notes or change summaries for the increment.
